newsitem.title: JAPAN: System in place to deal with any bank failures - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: System in place to deal with any bank failures - BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told parliament on Wednesday that a system has now been established in Japan to deal with any possible future failures at financial institutions.
Matsushita was responding to a question on whether the current system could deal with any future failure of a financial institution.
"If a financial institution fails in the future, a system which is now in place can cope with that," he said.
Matsushita added the BOJ will continue to provide the necessary funds to troubled financial institutions if they face liquidity problems in the course of their restructuring.
The planned revision of Japan's foreign exchange laws and implementation of "Big Bang" reforms will intensify competition among financial institutions, he said.
"The markets will select which institutions will survive," Matsushita said.
However, the reforms will also benefit the financial institutions by creating new business opportunities and a sound effective financial system, he said.
